The Experience
PresentationExcellentExcellentPoorGoodPoorGood
PackagingExcellentExcellentGoodGoodGoodGood
Field Research Verdict
  1. Joe & The Juice — Best overall experience, with standout bread, packaging, and a distinctive pesto and Tabasco sauce combination, despite having the highest price.
  2. Alforno — Strong overall competitor with special bread, good taste, excellent packaging, corn as an added vegetable, and the lowest price.
  3. Pain d’Or — Stands out for including corn, while maintaining a more traditional tuna sandwich profile with a moderate amount of mayonnaise.
  4. Espresso Lab — Offers a more distinctive vegetable component with cornichons instead of traditional pickles, along with a moderate amount of sauce.
  5. Stories — The excessive amount of sauce makes the tuna less visible and negatively affects the overall balance and presentation of the sandwich.
  6. Moulin d’Or — Uses a moderate amount of mayonnaise, but the sandwich is somewhat dry and could benefit from a slightly higher amount of sauce.
Vegetables: Pain d’Or and Alforno are the only competitors that include corn. Joe & The Juice offers jalapeños, while Espresso Lab uses cornichons instead of traditional pickles. Packaging: Joe & The Juice has the best overall packaging, with Alforno also standing out for its presentation. Bread & Taste: Joe & The Juice and Alforno both stood out for their special bread, which contributed to a better overall taste. Sauce: Stories uses an excessive amount of sauce, making the tuna less visible and affecting the overall balance of the sandwich. Joe & The Juice uses a combination of pesto and Tabasco sauce, while the other competitors use mayonnaise in more moderate amounts. Tuna Price: Joe & The Juice has the highest price, while Alforno offers the lowest price.
Summary of the numbers

Stories' price of 600,000 LBP is 3% below the median of the 5 competitors (621,000 LBP). Its length is 30 cm against a competitor median of 23.5 cm (28% larger), so per unit (per cm) it is 19% below the median. The larger portion widens the saving. The field team ranked Stories #5 of 6 on overall experience.

  • Labneh and Tuna — no weight or slice count recorded. The field team recorded length but no weight or slice count for these two items, so their value comparison is per cm only. No per-100g figure is estimated.
Packaging & presentation — field notes
AlfornoExcellentExcellent
  • The order came in a large paper bag. No Napkins were included. The sandwich had its own individual cardboard packaging. Overall, the packaging quality and presentation were very high.
Pain d’OrPoorGood
  • The order came in a standard large plastic bag, containing two large paper bags. Each paper bag contained 2–3 sandwiches grouped together, with each sandwich individually wrapped in paper. No cutlery was provided. Cheddar cheese was added as an add-on to the turkey sandwich, as it was available as an option on the menu.
StoriesPoorGood
  • Each sandwich was individually wrapped in paper packaging. No napkins or cutlery were provided with the order. The sandwich presentation was poor due to the excessive amount of mayonnaise and the limited amount of tuna. The tuna was barely visible, as it was heavily covered by the mayonnaise and vegetables.
Moulin d’OrGoodGood
  • Each sandwich was individually wrapped in paper and placed together with the other sandwiches in the same paper bag. No napkins were provided. The sandwich contained a moderate amount of mayonnaise, allowing the tuna to remain clearly visible and present in a good quantity. Overall, each sandwich had a good presentation.

The Experience
PresentationGoodExcellentGoodGoodGoodPoor
PackagingGoodExcellentPoorExcellentGoodGood
Field Research Verdict
  1. Alforno — Best Halloumi quality, highest sandwich weight, and lowest Halloumi price.
  2. Joe & The Juice — Best packaging, special bread, and very good overall taste; however, it has the highest Halloumi price.
  3. Pain d’Or — Only competitor to heat the sandwich, making the bread and Halloumi slightly warm and enhancing the overall taste.
  4. Starbucks — Special bread, good overall taste, and distinctive Zaatar sauce spread directly on the bread.
  5. Moulin d’Or — No major distinctive advantage identified; overall offering was average compared to the other competitors.
  6. Stories — Highest quantity and variety of vegetables, with good overall taste; however, the sandwich was noticeably oily due to the pesto sauce.
Sandwich Heating: The sandwich from Pain d’Or was the only one heated, making both the bread and Halloumi slightly warm, which enhanced the overall taste. Weight: Alforno has the highest sandwich weight, particularly for the Halloumi sandwich. Vegetables: Stories offers the highest quantity and variety of vegetables compared to the other competitors. Packaging: Joe & The Juice has the best overall packaging. Bread & Taste: Joe & The Juice and Starbucks both stood out for their special bread, which resulted in a better overall taste. Sauce: Starbucks’ Zaatar sauce is spread directly on the bread, adding a distinctive flavor to the sandwich. Halloumi Quality: Alforno had the best Halloumi quality among the competitors. Stories: Stories’ sandwich was noticeably oily due to the pesto sauce, but the overall taste was good. Halloumi Price: Joe & The Juice has the highest price for the Halloumi sandwich, while Alforno offers the lowest price.
Summary of the numbers

Stories' price of 550,000 LBP is 8% below the median of the 5 competitors (600,000 LBP). Its main-ingredient weight is 58 g against a competitor median of 43 g (35% larger), so per unit (per 100g of main ingredient) it is 24% below the median. The larger main-ingredient portion widens the saving. The field team ranked Stories #6 of 6 on overall experience.

  • Weight means the main ingredient, not the whole sandwich. The field team weighed the main ingredient only (the halloumi, chicken or rosto), and only for Halloumi, Chicken Caesar and Rosto. For those items the portion-adjusted figure is price per 100g of main ingredient; for every other item it is price per cm of sandwich.
  • Bread type set from the photos. The workbook recorded every Stories sandwich, and Alforno’s Rosto, on white bread. Checked against the photos with the client (6 Oct 2026): Stories’ Halloumi and Turkey & Cheese and Alforno’s Rosto come on a brown seeded loaf and are shown as Brown. Stories’ other sandwiches are on a white sesame baguette. Special breads (ciabatta, toast, Joe & The Juice’s special bread) are shown as recorded.
Packaging & presentation — field notes
Pain d’OrGoodPoor
  • The order came in a standard large plastic bag, containing two large paper bags. Each paper bag contained 2–3 sandwiches grouped together, with each sandwich individually wrapped in paper. However, the wrapping was quite loose, and the paper had already started coming off the sandwiches during unboxing. No cutlery was provided. Overall, the packaging was functional but lacked secure wrapping and presentation.
StarbucksGoodExcellent
  • The sandwich was wrapped in a plastic bag and placed on a cardboard tray inside the bag, which was then placed inside a paper bag. No napkins or cutlery were provided. Overall, the presentation was excellent.
StoriesPoorGood
  • Each sandwich was individually wrapped in paper packaging. No napkins or cutlery were provided with the order. The paper wrapping arrived heavily soiled with oil from the pesto sauce.

Field Research Verdict
  1. Alforno — Best overall taste, with the highest-quality chicken and a more balanced amount of Caesar sauce; despite Joe & The Juice using Tabasco and turkey bacon, Alforno was still tastier overall.
  2. Stories — Strong overall taste and the highest sandwich weight and vegetable variety, but the chicken smell was slightly unpleasant, likely because it was served warm, and the excessive Caesar sauce affected the balance.

Weight: Stories has the highest sandwich weight, particularly for the Chicken Caesar sandwich. Vegetables: Stories offers the highest quantity and variety of vegetables compared to the other competitors. Packaging: Joe & The Juice has the best overall packaging. Bread & Taste: Joe & The Juice stood out for its special bread, which contributed to a better overall taste. Sauce: The Caesar sauce was excessive in the Stories sandwich, while Alforno had a more moderate and balanced amount. Cheese: The cheese was clearly visible in the Alforno and Joe & The Juice sandwiches. In Stories, the cheese was not visibly present and was also not noticeable in the taste. Chicken Quality: Alforno had the best chicken quality among the competitors. Chicken Caesar Price: Joe & The Juice has the highest price for the sandwich, while Alforno offers the lowest price.
Summary of the numbers

Stories' price of 800,000 LBP is 17% below the median of the 2 competitors (969,000 LBP). Its main-ingredient weight is 75 g against a competitor median of 49 g (53% larger), so per unit (per 100g of main ingredient) it is 51% below the median. The larger main-ingredient portion widens the saving. The field team ranked Stories #2 of 3 on overall experience.

  • Joe & The Juice Chicken Caesar — chicken only, plus 12 g of turkey. The workbook lists 40 g of chicken and 12 g of turkey for this sandwich. Every figure and chart uses the chicken alone (40 g), like every other brand's main ingredient; Joe & The Juice's sandwich carries an additional 12 g of turkey protein on top, which is not counted.
  • Weight means the main ingredient, not the whole sandwich. The field team weighed the main ingredient only (the halloumi, chicken or rosto), and only for Halloumi, Chicken Caesar and Rosto. For those items the portion-adjusted figure is price per 100g of main ingredient; for every other item it is price per cm of sandwich.

Field Research Verdict
  1. Joe & The Juice — Best overall sandwich, with the strongest bread, cheese quality, packaging, and unique pesto sauce, despite having the highest price.
  2. Alforno — Strong value for money, offering the best turkey quality at the lowest price.
  3. Stories — Offers the highest number of slices, but excessive mayonnaise affects the taste and the portion is difficult to compare by weight.
  4. Espresso Lab — Offers a relatively small portion compared to its price, with the sandwich essentially being a toast cut in half.
  5. Pain d’Or — Less competitive as the cheese is not included in the sandwich and must be ordered as an add-on.
  6. Moulin d’Or
Number of Slices: Stories has the highest number of slices in the sandwich. However, its slices are cut differently from the other competitors, so the number of slices alone does not indicate the largest portion by weight. Packaging: Joe & The Juice has the best overall packaging, with a more appealing and well-presented format. Bread & Taste: Joe & The Juice stood out for its special bread, which contributed to a better overall taste and eating experience. Sauce: The excessive amount of mayonnaise in the Stories sandwich affects the overall taste and balance of the sandwich. Turkey Quality: Alforno had the best turkey quality among the competitors, standing out in terms of taste and overall quality. Cheese Quality: Joe & The Juice had the best cheese quality, using fresh mozzarella, which enhanced the overall taste and quality of the sandwich. Turkey & Cheese Price: Joe & The Juice has the highest price for the Turkey & Cheese sandwich, while Alforno offers the lowest price. Portion Size: Espresso Lab ranked second in terms of pricing, while its sandwich is relatively small compared to the other competitors. It consists of a toast cut in half, resulting in a smaller overall portion. Add-ons: All competitors included cheese as part of the sandwich recipe, with the exception of Pain d’Or, where the cheese had to be ordered as an add-on. Pesto Sauce: Joe & The Juice was the only competitor to use pesto sauce.
Summary of the numbers
  • Turkey & Cheese — measured by turkey slices. This item was recorded by the number of turkey slices rather than weight (the count is slices of turkey, client-confirmed 6 Oct 2026), so a per-turkey-slice figure is shown alongside per cm. It appears as a separate marker in the dashboard and is never substituted for the main metric.
  • Moulin d’Or ranked sixth. Moulin d’Or was priced and photographed but left out of the original verdict; the client has since ranked it #6 of 6 (6 Oct 2026). No written reason was recorded for it.
  • Bread type set from the photos. The workbook recorded every Stories sandwich, and Alforno’s Rosto, on white bread. Checked against the photos with the client (6 Oct 2026): Stories’ Halloumi and Turkey & Cheese and Alforno’s Rosto come on a brown seeded loaf and are shown as Brown. Stories’ other sandwiches are on a white sesame baguette. Special breads (ciabatta, toast, Joe & The Juice’s special bread) are shown as recorded.

Experience & value

Presentation and Packaging are the field team's tiers (Poor / Good / Excellent), scored 0 / 0.5 / 1 on the radar. Quadrants: Value leader = cheaper per portion than the median with experience at or above it; Premium = pricier, at or above; Weak = cheaper, below; Overpriced = pricier, below.   • Stories Brownie — cheapest on the shelf, dearest per 100g. Stories' Brownie is the lowest-priced (350,000 LBP) but also the smallest: 41 g against 65–82 g for the competitors.   • Which brownie is heaviest. The field team's verdict describes Joe & The Juice's brownie as having “the highest weight”. Field Research Verdict
  1. Joe & The Juice — Despite having the lowest weight, it was the tastiest option, with a soft and fluffy texture and chocolate chips on top.
  2. Starbucks — Had a more appealing presentation than Stories and was well filled with chocolate inside.
  3. Stories — Had a less appealing exterior presentation, while the inside was dry and lacked noticeable chocolate filling.
Summary of the numbers

Stories' price of 350,000 LBP is 22% below the median of the 2 competitors (446,000 LBP). Its portion is 101 g against a competitor median of 83.5 g (21% larger), so per unit (per 100g) it is 40% below the median. The larger portion widens the saving. The field team ranked Stories #3 of 3 on overall experience.

Field Research Verdict
  1. Stories — Had a soft texture that was easy to bite into, with an appealing presentation and an enjoyable, tasty flavor.
  2. Cremino — Was very hard and difficult to break, with a lower level of sweetness and a less enjoyable overall texture.
  3. Wooden Bakery — Arrived slightly stale and crumbled easily, with a less enjoyable taste.
Summary of the numbers

Stories' price of 400,000 LBP is 299% above the median of the 2 competitors (100,182 LBP). Its portion is 84 g against a competitor median of 54 g (56% larger), so per unit (per 100g) it is 165% above the median. The larger portion narrows the premium but does not close it. The field team ranked Stories #1 of 3 on overall experience.

  • Wooden Bakery Sablet — a genuinely low price. Wooden Bakery's Sablet is priced at 40,365 LBP for 51 g — the price as recorded by the field team and verified as correct, not a data-entry error. That works out to 79,147 LBP per 100g, against 280,702–476,190 for the other Sablets, so it is an outlier in the Sablet charts and pulls the market median down.

Experience & value

Presentation and Packaging are the field team's tiers (Poor / Good / Excellent), scored 0 / 0.5 / 1 on the radar. Price and Portion value are each brand's gap to the competitor median, so cheaper plots further out; the median sits at 0.5. Client rank is the position inside each item's own ranking, not an averaged rank. The category view takes the median across items. Quadrants: Value leader = cheaper per portion than the median with experience at or above it; Premium = pricier, at or above; Weak = cheaper, below; Overpriced = pricier, below. A tie with the median counts as at-or-better; the rule is identical for every brand.

  • Pastries were generally provided in boxes, but the box size was not consistent with the pastry size. Some boxes were significantly larger than the pastry, while others fit the pastry appropriately.
  • In some cases, paper was placed underneath the pastry, but it became damaged when the pastry came into contact with the box cover or shifted inside the box due to excess space.
  • Some pastries were well positioned and presented, while others were grouped together in the same box, affecting their individual presentation.
  • The pastry boxes were placed inside a paper bag for delivery.
  • Cutlery packaging was incomplete: a fork and knife were provided without a napkin, and the cutlery was placed directly inside the paper bag rather than being properly packaged.

The Experience
Presentation (deduced from the field notes)GoodGoodGoodExcellent
PackagingGoodGoodGoodExcellent
Field Research Verdict
  1. Starbucks — Best overall. The caramel flavor was very strong and enjoyable, with a fresh taste. The drink was also highly visually appealing, with an attractive color that gave a caramel-popcorn vibe. The overall visual presentation and cup design also enhanced the experience and made the drink more appealing psychologically.
  2. Stories — Very close to Starbucks in terms of taste and overall enjoyable. However, it was slightly less visually appealing, and the caramel flavor was a little lighter than Starbucks.
  3. Dunkin — Good caramel flavor and overall tasty.
  4. Espresso Lab — Average overall and not particularly enjoyable.
Summary of the numbers

Stories' price of 500,000 LBP is 17% below the median of the 3 competitors (599,000 LBP). Its stated cup size is 16 oz against a competitor median of 14 oz (14% larger), so per unit (per oz) it is 25% below the median. The larger cup widens the saving. The field team ranked Stories #2 of 4 when tasting the drinks.

  • Cup sizes differ. Each brand's cup is the size it sells under that name: Stories Medium 16 oz; Starbucks Medium 16 oz; Dunkin Medium 14 oz; Espresso Lab Medium 12 oz. The ounces are the cup's stated size as filed, not a measured fill. Price per oz adjusts for the difference in size.
  • Range per oz. Espresso Lab costs the most per oz (49,917 LBP: 599,000 LBP for 12 oz); Stories costs the least (31,250 LBP: 500,000 LBP for 16 oz).
  • Presentation tier deduced from the field notes. The workbook rates packaging only. At the client's instruction (7 Oct 2026) each brand's Presentation tier is deduced from the field team's own description: Stories Good (“Good packaging and overall presentation”); Starbucks Good (“good presentation and practical packaging”); Dunkin Good (“Good packaging and presentation”); Espresso Lab Excellent (“Excellent packaging and overall presentation”).

Field Research Verdict
  1. Stories — Ranked first for taste because the matcha powder used is already sweetened. Most competitors’ matcha drinks are bitter unless additional sugar is added, while Stories’ version is more balanced and enjoyable as served.
  2. Espresso Lab — Not very bitter and overall tasty, although it still benefits from some added sweetness.
  3. Starbucks — Not overly bitter, but difficult to enjoy without adding sugar.
  4. Joe & The Juice — Similar to Starbucks; the matcha powder is quite bitter when served without added sugar.
  5. Dunkin — Not enjoyable overall; the drink was bitter, and the bitterness itself was unpleasant.
Summary of the numbers

Stories' price of 550,000 LBP is 7% below the median of the 4 competitors (588,500 LBP). Its stated cup size is 20 oz against a competitor median of 16 oz (25% larger), so per unit (per oz) it is 29% below the median. The larger cup widens the saving. The field team ranked Stories #1 of 5 when tasting the drinks.

  • Cup sizes differ. Each brand's cup is the size it sells under that name: Stories Large 20 oz; Starbucks Large 20 oz; Espresso Lab Large 16 oz; Joe & The Juice Medium 16 oz; Dunkin Medium 14 oz. The ounces are the cup's stated size as filed, not a measured fill. Price per oz adjusts for the difference in size.
  • Range per oz. Espresso Lab costs the most per oz (46,875 LBP: 750,000 LBP for 16 oz); Stories and Starbucks cost the least (27,500 LBP: 550,000 LBP for 20 oz).

At the client's instruction (7 Oct 2026) each brand's Presentation tier is deduced from the field team's own description: Stories Good (“Good packaging and overall presentation”); Starbucks Good (“good presentation and practical packaging”); Dunkin Good (“Good packaging and presentation”); Espresso Lab Excellent (“Excellent packaging and overall presentation”); Joe & The Juice Excellent (“Excellent packaging and overall presentation”).

PackagingGoodExcellentGoodExcellentGood
Field Research Verdict
  1. Starbucks — Best overall. The drink was well-balanced, not overly sweet or bitter, with a very enjoyable overall taste.
  2. Espresso Lab — Tasty and enjoyable, but slightly sweeter than Starbucks.
  3. Stories — Overly sweet. It may appeal to those who prefer sweeter drinks, but the taste was not consistent, varying from bitter to sweeter across different orders.
  4. Joe & The Juice — Not enjoyable overall; the drink was noticeably more bitter than sweet.
  5. Dunkin — Not tasty overall.
Summary of the numbers

Stories' price of 500,000 LBP is 14% below the median of the 4 competitors (583,500 LBP). Its stated cup size is 16 oz against a competitor median of 13 oz (23% larger), so per unit (per oz) it is 30% below the median. The larger cup widens the saving. The field team ranked Stories #3 of 5 when tasting the drinks.

  • Cup sizes differ. Each brand's cup is the size it sells under that name: Stories Medium 16 oz; Starbucks Medium 16 oz; Dunkin Medium 14 oz; Espresso Lab Medium 12 oz; Joe & The Juice Small 12 oz. The ounces are the cup's stated size as filed, not a measured fill. Price per oz adjusts for the difference in size.
  • Range per oz. Espresso Lab costs the most per oz (62,500 LBP: 750,000 LBP for 12 oz); Stories and Starbucks cost the least (31,250 LBP: 500,000 LBP for 16 oz).
  • Presentation tier deduced from the field notes. The workbook rates packaging only. At the client's instruction (7 Oct 2026) each brand's Presentation tier is deduced from the field team's own description: Stories Good (“Good packaging and overall presentation”); Starbucks Good (“good presentation and practical packaging”); Dunkin Good (“Good packaging and presentation”); Espresso Lab Excellent (“Excellent packaging and overall presentation”); Joe & The Juice Excellent (“Excellent packaging and overall presentation”).
  • Joe & The Juice — a different drink. Joe & The Juice has no White Mocha; the branch sent an Iced Mocha, filed in its Small 12 oz cup. It is priced and ranked as filed, but it is not the same drink, so its price is not like-for-like with the others.

Experience & value

Presentation and Packaging are the field team's tiers (Poor / Good / Excellent), scored 0 / 0.5 / 1 on the radar. The workbook rates packaging only, so Presentation is deduced from the field team's packaging and presentation notes. Price and Portion value are each brand's gap to the competitor median, so cheaper plots further out; the median sits at 0.5. Client rank is the position inside each item's own ranking, not an averaged rank. The category view takes the median across items. Quadrants: Value leader = cheaper per portion than the median with experience at or above it; Premium = pricier, at or above; Weak = cheaper, below; Overpriced = pricier, below. A tie with the median counts as at-or-better; the rule is identical for every brand.

Summary of the numbers — all three sizes
  • Small, Medium and Large are each brand's own sizes. Each column is the cup the brand sells under that name, so cups of the same name differ in weight (Small 95–157 g; Medium 125–202 g; Large 164–315 g), and the flavour bought differs by brand. Price per 100g adjusts for the difference in size.
  • Expected size against actual size. The workbook records each cup's expected size in ounces and its actual size, the recorded weight in ounces (1 oz = 28.35 g). 10 of 11 cups weigh less than their expected size; Stories' three cups are −18% to −24%, and the furthest under is Cremino's Large (−31%). The table shows the difference for every cup; the charts use the weight in grams. Weights are the yogurt alone: the toppings came separately and were not weighed (client, 7 Oct 2026), so price per 100g is per 100g of yogurt.
  • Toppings are counted in portions. One topping is one spoon. “(2)” after a topping means two portions of it were ordered, and the count row is portions, not different toppings: Pinkberry's 5 are 5 portions of mango and chocolate sauce.
  • Presentation tier deduced from the field notes. The workbook rates packaging only. At the client's instruction (7 Oct 2026) each brand's Presentation tier is deduced from the field team's own packaging and presentation description: Stories Good (“Good presentation and packaging”); Fro.U Excellent (“Excellent packaging and presentation”); Cremino Poor (“not visually appealing”, “cheap, low-quality impression”); Pinkberry Good (a “distinctive puffed lid”, against toppings, tissues and spoons placed loosely in the bag and a lid that “easily collapsed”).
  • Taste applies to every size of a flavour. The field team tasted each flavour once (Mango, Plain, Chocolate); the result holds for every cup size of that flavour (client, 7 Oct 2026). Each cup's taste rank is shown in the size tables; the cup sizes themselves carry no overall rank, because the brands in one size were bought in different flavours. Fro.U was ranked for Mango only, so its Speculoos & Original cup has no taste rank; Pinkberry's Black Berry was not ranked.

Field Research Verdict — taste, by flavour
Mango
  1. Fro.U — More natural and well-balanced; not overly sweet while still having a clear mango flavor.
  2. Stories — Noticeably sweeter and more artificial-tasting; less balanced and can feel too sweet after a few bites.
Plain
  1. Pinkberry — Very well-balanced, not overly sweet, and very tasty overall.
  2. Cremino — Slightly lighter in sweetness compared to Pinkberry, with a good overall taste.
  3. Stories — Even though it is a plain flavor, it still tastes noticeably sweet.
Chocolate
  1. Pinkberry — Richer and tastier overall.
  2. Stories — Good, but less enjoyable compared to Pinkberry.

Experience & value

Presentation and Packaging are the field team's tiers (Poor / Good / Excellent), scored 0 / 0.5 / 1 on the radar. The workbook rates packaging only, so Presentation is deduced from the field team's packaging and presentation notes. Price and Portion value are each brand's gap to the competitor median, so cheaper plots further out; the median sits at 0.5. Client rank is the position inside each item's own ranking, not an averaged rank. The category view takes the median across items. Quadrants: Value leader = cheaper per portion than the median with experience at or above it; Premium = pricier, at or above; Weak = cheaper, below; Overpriced = pricier, below. A tie with the median counts as at-or-better; the rule is identical for every brand. Not shown (no data recorded): Client rank.

The Experience
PresentationExcellentExcellentExcellentExcellentExcellentExcellent
PackagingGoodGoodExcellentExcellentExcellentExcellent
Field Research Verdict
  1. Grab n Go — Tender, tasty chicken and a very good dressing, in a divided box with every ingredient kept separate; no cutlery was provided.
  2. Wooden Bakery — Good packaging and presentation and plenty of croutons; the chicken was slightly dry and the sauce sharp.
  3. Stories — Fully sealed with the dressing on the side, visible Parmesan and cherry tomatoes and a tasty dressing; but the chicken had an unpleasant, rancid smell.
  4. Urban Fresh — A large, pleasant-smelling chicken breast, plenty of cheese and avocado; the dressing container had no expiry date.
  5. Pain d’Or — Very dry chicken in a small portion and a watery, weak dressing.
  6. Zaatar w Zeit — Extremely hard, dry chicken, and Parmesan barely visible.
Reasons summarised from each brand's notes in the field workbook; the ranking order is the field team's.
Summary of the numbers

Stories' price of 900,000 LBP is in line with the median of the 5 competitors (897,000 LBP). Its portion is 325 g against a competitor median of 248 g (31% larger), so per unit (per 100g) it is 23% below the median. At a shelf price in line with the market, the larger portion makes it cheaper per unit. The field team ranked Stories #3 of 6 on overall experience.

  • Two weights: the whole salad and its main ingredient. The field team weighed each salad as sold (net weight) and, separately, its main ingredient — the chicken, halloumi or feta. Price per 100g uses the net weight of the whole salad, recorded for every brand. Price per 100g of main ingredient is shown in the table only where it was weighed; it was not weighed for Tuna Pasta or the Caesar Salad without chicken, nor for Stories' Pasta Pesto, which has no chicken.
  • Stories Chicken Caesar — by far the largest chicken portion (confirmed). Stories' chicken alone was weighed at 147 g — the field team confirmed this is the chicken only, not the salad — against 26–75 g for the competitors (next largest: Urban Fresh, 75 g). Per 100g of chicken it is therefore the cheapest, at 612,245 LBP against 1,200,000–2,423,077 LBP. The field notes for the same salad record that the chicken had an unpleasant, rancid smell.

Field Research Verdict
  1. Joe & The Juice — A great variety of vegetables, fruits and seeds, with tasty chicken and dressing, though little dressing.
  2. Grab n Go — Described as the tastiest, with a distinctive pomegranate flavour, well-cooked chicken, fresh greens and a well-portioned dressing; no cutlery was provided.
  3. Urban Fresh — Well packaged, with seasoned chicken, white quinoa with plenty of nuts, and a tasty dressing.
Reasons summarised from each brand's notes in the field workbook; the ranking order is the field team's.
Summary of the numbers
  • Two weights: the whole salad and its main ingredient. The field team weighed each salad as sold (net weight) and, separately, its main ingredient — the chicken, halloumi or feta. Price per 100g uses the net weight of the whole salad, recorded for every brand. Price per 100g of main ingredient is shown in the table only where it was weighed; it was not weighed for Tuna Pasta or the Caesar Salad without chicken, nor for Stories' Pasta Pesto, which has no chicken.
  • Stories not in this comparison. The field team priced this salad for competitors only, so there is no Stories price to compare. It is shown as a market reference and is not part of the Salads dashboard.
Packaging & presentation — field notes
Joe & The JuiceExcellentGood
  • Great variety of vegetables, fruits, and seeds.
  • Chicken was tasty.
  • Dressing was also tasty, but the quantity was limited.
  • Cutlery was provided with the salad.
  • Dressings were labeled and served separately in sealed containers, but no expiry date was indicated.
  • A tissue was placed inside the paper bag underneath the salads to help protect the packaging.
Grab n GoExcellentGood
  • The tastiest among all competitors, with a distinctive pomegranate flavor.
  • Chicken was well-cooked, white, and had a pleasant smell.
  • Quinoa was very tasty, and all greens were fresh.
  • Dressing was well-balanced and perfectly portioned.
  • No cutlery was provided.
  • The dressing container was labeled.
  • An expiry date was indicated on the salad packaging.
Urban FreshExcellentExcellent
  • Well-packaged with good overall presentation.
  • Chicken was yellowish in color, with visible seasoning.
  • White quinoa with a good amount of nuts.
  • Dressing was tasty.
  • The salad was served with cutlery.
  • The dressing container was labeled without expiry date.
  • An expiry date was indicated on the salad packaging.

Experience & value

Presentation and Packaging are the field team's tiers (Poor / Good / Excellent), scored 0 / 0.5 / 1 on the radar. Price and Portion value are each brand's gap to the competitor median, so cheaper plots further out; the median sits at 0.5. Client rank is the position inside each item's own ranking, not an averaged rank. The category view takes the median across items. Quadrants: Value leader = cheaper per portion than the median with experience at or above it; Premium = pricier, at or above; Weak = cheaper, below; Overpriced = pricier, below. A tie with the median counts as at-or-better; the rule is identical for every brand.
